items.text: AI, automation and integration. We build the fix into how you already work, not bolted on beside it. AI where it earns its keep, automation for the repetitive, integration so your tools finally talk. Shipped in weeks, owned by your team, measured against the hours it returns.

props.headline: Where your sector quietly
props.body: Every industry loses time in its own way. These are the leaks unique to each sector, and we leave no stone unturned. Seven worlds we know well:

items.title: Real estate
items.text: Less time on portals, more time closing. Comps and area research by hand, re-listing the same property across every portal, chasing solicitors and surveyors, matching new stock to buyers manually.

items.title: Healthcare
items.text: Less time on admin, more time on patients. Re-typing patient details across disconnected systems, chasing no-shows, coding claims by hand, compiling compliance reports from scratch.

items.title: Education
items.text: Less time on paperwork, more time teaching. Re-keying enrolment data across SIS, LMS and finance, building timetables by hand, chasing consent forms, collating attendance and progress.

items.title: Financial services
items.text: Less time reconciling, more time advising. Manual KYC and onboarding checks, re-keying figures between spreadsheets and core systems, assembling client statements, pulling together regulatory packs.

items.title: Manufacturing
items.text: Less time on the clipboard, more time on the line. Re-entering orders between ERP, shop floor and accounts, tracking stock on spreadsheets, logging quality checks by hand, rebuilding downtime reports.

items.title: Professional services
items.text: Less time on the timesheet, more time on the work. Reconstructing billable hours from memory, drafting near-identical proposals, chasing late payments, copying client data between CRM and delivery tools.

items.title: Retail and hospitality
items.text: Less time behind the scenes, more time with guests. Reconciling sales across POS, online and marketplaces, re-keying stock counts, building rotas by hand, stitching together weekly footfall reports.
